automations.reported_overdue_falsely_note: state/heartbeat.json said OVERDUE for this row at 06:15Z. It is not stopped: list_triggers shows enabled true, cron 55 * * * *, last fired 05:55:38Z — twenty minutes before the alarm — and next run 06:55Z. The alarm is an artifact of WHERE the detector looks. This row has no liveness block, so the only mark available is last_fired_at in this file, and this file is only refreshed by a lap that happens to hold MCP tools. Between such laps the mark ages while the automation keeps firing, and the detector cannot tell that apart from a stopped trigger. RUNBOOK 3 tells a lap to treat overdue as its TOP priority, so a false alarm here does not merely mislead — it redirects the scarce pool. The repair is a liveness mark the automation itself moves, the way codex-loop moves state/codex-lane.json; the cookie loop pushes to a different repository, so that mark has to be something this repo can see, and nobody has priced that.
automations.reported_overdue_falsely_2_note: SECOND false overdue on this row in one day, and it is what got the detector fixed rather than the row. The 09:15Z run of check-heartbeats said OVERDUE at 224 minutes; list_triggers at 09:35Z shows enabled true, cron 55 * * * *, fired 08:56:07Z — nineteen minutes before the alarm — and next 09:55Z. Its own prior note named the repair as a liveness mark the automation itself moves and priced it as unowned, because the cookie loop pushes to another repository. That repair is still unowned. What was buildable from here is the DETECTOR admitting the limit: scripts/check-heartbeats.mjs classify() now returns mark_stale instead of overdue when the only mark is a scheduler snapshot taken BEFORE the deadline it would have to prove, and reports it with its own count and instruction. The exemption is not blanket — a snapshot refreshed after the deadline that still shows the old fire reads overdue, and tests/run-tests.mjs goes red if either half is removed.

automations.cadence_measured_from: GitHub Actions run history for codex-inbox.yml, 26 runs total, read through the API rather than inferred from state files

cadence_measurement.what_it_says: The cron reads 41 * * * * and GitHub delivers it 15 to 37 minutes late EVERY time — the minute in the cron is not a minute this workflow has ever started on. More important than the lateness is the SKIPPING: two gaps of 174 and 132 minutes, both in the most recent stretch, so the schedule drops runs rather than merely delaying them. 11 scheduled runs in 13.1 hours is 0.84 per hour against a cron asking for 1.
cadence_measurement.why_the_cadence_moved_to_90: check-heartbeats calls a row overdue at twice its cadence, so cadence 60 meant an alarm at 120 minutes — and two of the ten observed gaps were longer than that. The detector would have reported the lane STOPPED twice today while it was merely late, which is the same false-alarm class cookie-daily produced this hour, except this one is predictable from the data. 90 puts the alarm at 180 minutes, six minutes above the largest gap observed.
cadence_measurement.the_margin_is_thin_and_that_is_deliberat: Six minutes over an observed maximum drawn from ten gaps is not a safety margin, it is the smallest number the evidence supports. A larger cadence would silence real stops for longer. If a third gap over 180 minutes appears, the honest response is to raise this again WITH the new number, not to have pre-emptively padded it — and if the lane genuinely stops, the alarm should fire while the queue still matters.
cadence_measurement.what_this_does_not_fix: The cadence is still a hand-written number compared against a hand-refreshed mark. Nothing derives it from the run history automatically; a lap with GitHub access had to read 26 runs to produce it. That is the same shape as the registry gap above, one level down.

reconciliation_note: cadence/enabled for claude-trigger rows are reconciled against list_triggers, not asserted here. Actions cannot call that API, so a lap with MCP is the only thing that can refresh them — check observed_at before trusting these fields. 2026-08-10: the two readings 58 minutes apart were wrong in opposite directions, which is the measurement behind check-heartbeats.mjs unverifiedReservations() and the registry age pacing.mjs now prints. Note what that check cannot do — at 66 minutes old the registry was inside every reasonable staleness window and already wrong. Age bounds silent drift; it does not detect the world changing. Only list_triggers does, and only a lap can call it.
reconciliation_gap_nobody_has_closed: The reservation that dominates pacing — youtube-loop and cookie-daily at a derived upper bound each, capped to 16.80% — rests on rows only an MCP lap can verify. Between MCP laps the scheduler can change and nothing here would know. Actions cannot see it. Nobody has priced a workaround, and this line exists so the next lap does not rediscover the gap as if it were new.
how_to_reconcile_cheaply: PREFER list_sessions OVER list_triggers. Measured 2026-08-10T12:46Z: list_triggers returns each Routine's ENTIRE prompt body, and one page of 25 rows returned roughly forty thousand characters of other loops' instructions, most of it a months-old ELDRIA backlog with nothing to do with this registry. It cost more context than the whole rest of the lap and answered one field. list_sessions returns titles, tags, created_at and status — and for any trigger whose job is to CREATE a session, the session it created is better evidence than the trigger's own last_fired_at, because it shows the firing produced something rather than merely occurring. Use list_triggers only for a trigger that creates no session, and prefer a targeted lookup over a page when you can.
